Extract Transcript Sequences into an Annotation Directory

Source: R/sequences.R
transcript_sequences.Rd

Adds the spliced sequence of every transcript of an annotation directory as annot_data_sequences.parquet, read by transcript_orfs(), coding_potential() and the sequence-aware rules of transcript_productivity(). Sequences come either from a genome FASTA (genome_fasta; exons are cut out of each chromosome, reverse complemented on the minus strand and concatenated in transcript order, so novel transcripts from long-read or assembly annotations are covered) or from a transcript FASTA (transcript_fasta, for example the GENCODE transcripts.fa.gz; sequences are matched by the first token of the header, with and without the identifier version).

The genome is streamed in chunks (plain or gzip-compressed FASTA, no index needed) and only one chromosome is held in memory at a time; a human genome takes a few minutes. Chromosome names are matched to the annotation seqid directly, or after adding or removing a chr prefix. Soft-masked (lower-case) bases are upper-cased.

Usage

extract_transcript_sequences(
  x,
  genome_fasta = NULL,
  transcript_fasta = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  chunk_bytes = 6.4e+07
)

has_sequences(x)

transcript_sequences(x, transcript_id = NULL)

Arguments

x

An annotation directory path or an IsoformicExperiment.

genome_fasta

Path to a genome FASTA file (.fa, .fa.gz), see download_reference(file_type = "genome_fasta").

transcript_fasta

Path to a transcript FASTA file, see download_reference(file_type = "fasta").

overwrite

Logical, replace existing sequences (default FALSE).

chunk_bytes

Number of bytes read per chunk while streaming (default 64 MB).

transcript_id

Optional transcript identifiers to read; NULL reads all sequences.

Value

The path of the written Parquet file, invisibly. The table has columns transcript_id, sequence and seq_length.

Details

The sequences table is optional: annotation directories without it keep working, and has_sequences() tells whether it is present. Transcripts whose chromosome is absent from the FASTA (or whose identifier is absent from a transcript FASTA) are reported and left out.

See also

transcript_orfs(), coding_potential()

Examples

gff <- system.file("extdata", "example.gff3", package = "isoformic")
fasta <- system.file("extdata", "example_transcripts.fa.gz", package = "isoformic")
annot <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(gff, output_path = tempdir(), annot_name = "seq_demo")
#> ℹ Parsing example.gff3 (GFF) into /tmp/RtmpmIi7db/seq_demo.
extract_transcript_sequences(annot, transcript_fasta = fasta, overwrite = TRUE)
#> ✔ Wrote 72 transcript sequences to
#>   /tmp/RtmpmIi7db/seq_demo/annot_data_sequences.parquet.
has_sequences(annot)
#> [1] TRUE
head(transcript_sequences(annot)[, c("transcript_id", "seq_length")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 2
#>   transcript_id     seq_length
#>   <chr>                  <int>
#> 1 ENST00000282397.9       7123
#> 2 ENST00000615611.4       1476
#> 3 ENST00000617835.4        434
#> 4 ENST00000543394.2       1275
#> 5 ENST00000540678.2       1927
#> 6 ENST00000541932.5       2969

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# From a genome FASTA (covers novel transcripts of any annotation)
genome <- download_reference(version = "49", file_type = "genome_fasta", region = "primary")
extract_transcript_sequences(annot, genome_fasta = genome)
} # }
